idiom_name: named invariant predicate checked at construction and after every mutation
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: give the state owner a side-effect-free predicate method that states the invariant in domain terms, call it at the end of every constructor and at the exit of every state-changing operation, and make the failure loud (abort, exception or assertion error) rather than recoverable. Preconditions on public entry points are checked before the operation starts, postconditions and invariants after it ends. Where the language compiles the check away, mirror each predicate with a test that invokes it directly, and where the rule can be expressed in the type system, prefer that.
code_sketch:
class Order:
    def check_invariants(self):
        assert self.total == sum(line.amount for line in self.lines)
        assert self.status != CANCELLED or not self.is_shipped()

    def add_line(self, line):
        assert not self.is_shipped()          # trusted-caller precondition
        next_total = self.total + line.amount
        assert next_total >= 0                 # validate candidate before mutation
        self.lines.append(line)
        self.total = next_total
        self.check_invariants()               # postcondition / class invariant
pitfalls: Writing a predicate that mutates or caches state; assertions may be compiled out, so the object behaves differently between debug and release.
Checking only in the constructor: state changed through mutators escapes the invariant.
Making the failure recoverable, which turns a broken model into a silently corrupt one.
In async contexts (async/await, thread pools), catching and swallowing a panic/assertion failure silently drops the request or task with no visible error in logs or metrics.
Using assert() for input validation: when the language strips assertions in optimized builds (-O, NDEBUG), input validation disappears and invalid data enters the domain.
